words.sense: believes effort cannot alter what is fated to occur
misconceptions: Caused events can still change when people change the causes.

words.sense: believes outcomes arise from prior causes rather than uncaused choice
misconceptions: Believing an outcome is unavoidable regardless of action is not simply tracing causes.

semantic_axes.description: A fatalist thinks effort cannot change the destined result; a determinist thinks events, including choices, follow preceding causes.

edges.boundary_rule: A fatalist thinks effort cannot change the destined result; a determinist thinks events, including choices, follow preceding causes.
irrelevant_clues: how long they discuss the problem

misconceptions.M1: Caused events can still change when people change the causes.
misconceptions.M2: Believing an outcome is unavoidable regardless of action is not simply tracing causes.
misconceptions.M3: Do not stick with an old answer after decisive evidence changes, or let surface distractions override the boundary.

beats.text: Rohan argued that his exam result was already settled and studying could not affect it.
beats.decisive_clue: belief that effort cannot alter a fixed outcome
beats.reason: He considers the result fixed despite possible action.

beats.text: He said even a perfect week of revision would leave the mark unchanged.
beats.decisive_clue: belief that even major effort cannot alter the outcome
beats.reason: The revision example makes his rejection of effective effort explicit.

chains.feedback_short: The key is belief that even major effort cannot alter the outcome; the revision example makes his rejection of effective effort explicit.
chains.feedback_deep: Fatalist concerns believes effort cannot alter what is fated to occur; determinist concerns believes outcomes arise from prior causes rather than uncaused choice. The revision example makes his rejection of effective effort explicit.
chains.contrast_rule: Fatalist: effort makes no difference; determinist: decisions have earlier causes.

beats.text: Elsa said every outcome, including a person's decisions, follows from earlier conditions rather than arising without causes.
beats.decisive_clue: belief that all outcomes and decisions follow prior causes
beats.reason: She applies causal necessity to outcomes and human decisions.

beats.text: She added that changing the watering schedule would change the results because it would change one of the prior conditions.
beats.decisive_clue: belief that changing a prior cause changes the determined outcome
beats.reason: She treats intervention as part of the causal chain, not as impossible or irrelevant.

chains.feedback_short: The key is that all outcomes and decisions follow prior causes; changing a cause can therefore change the result.
chains.feedback_deep: A fatalist thinks effort cannot alter a fated result; a determinist thinks events, including choices, follow prior causes. Elsa treats intervention as part of that causal chain.
chains.contrast_rule: Fatalist: effort makes no difference; determinist: decisions and outcomes have earlier causes.

beats.text: Clara argued that habits and earlier experiences shape every decision a person makes.
beats.decisive_clue: belief that choices emerge from preceding influences
beats.reason: She treats human decisions as causally produced.

beats.text: She said even deciding to resist a habit has its own earlier causes.
beats.decisive_clue: belief that even attempts to change have earlier causes
beats.reason: Including resistance shows the principle applies to choices as well.

chains.feedback_short: The key is belief that even attempts to change have earlier causes; including resistance shows the principle applies to choices as well.
chains.feedback_deep: Fatalist concerns believes effort cannot alter what is fated to occur; determinist concerns believes outcomes arise from prior causes rather than uncaused choice. Including resistance shows the principle applies to choices as well.
chains.contrast_rule: Fatalist: effort makes no difference; determinist: decisions have earlier causes.

beats.text: Yuna argued that attendance and students' decisions about attending are determined by earlier routines, bus schedules, and family arrangements.
beats.decisive_clue: belief that behavior and decisions follow prior conditions
beats.reason: She treats attendance choices as causally produced by earlier circumstances.

beats.text: She added that a later bus could improve attendance by changing one of those determining conditions.
beats.decisive_clue: belief that changing a prior cause changes the resulting behavior
beats.reason: The schedule change is itself a cause in the process she describes.

chains.feedback_short: The key is that attendance decisions follow prior conditions; changing one of those conditions can change the result.
chains.feedback_deep: A fatalist thinks effort cannot alter a fated result; a determinist thinks events, including choices, follow prior causes. Yuna treats the bus schedule as one cause in that process.
chains.contrast_rule: Fatalist: effort makes no difference; determinist: decisions and outcomes have earlier causes.
